newsitem.title: INDIA: Highlights of farm sector in India Economic Survey.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of farm sector in India Economic Survey.

text.p: NEW DELHI, Feb 25 (Reuter) _ Following are the highlights of India's agriculture sector in the annual Economic Survey for 1996/97, tabled in parliament by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Tuesday.
* Foodgrains output in 1996/97 (June-July) expected to rise to 191.2 million tonnes from 185 million in 1995/96.
* Rice output in 1996/97 forecast at 79.6 million tonnes, same as in 1995/96.
* Wheat output in 1996/97 expected at 64.5 million tonnes, up from 62.6 million in 1995/96.
* Oilseeds output in 1996/97 expected to rise to 24.1 million tonnes from 22.4 million in 1995/96.
* Soybean output in 1996/97 forecast at 5.11 million, marginally up from 4.99 million in the same period in 1995/96.
* Groundnut production in 1996/97 expected to be 9.12 million tonnes, sharply up from 7.81 million in 1995/96.
* Sugarcane output in 1996/97 expected to fall to 273.6 million tonnes from 283 million in 1995/96.
* Cotton output in 1996/97 expected to be 14.3 million bales (one bale equals 170 kg) compared with 13.1 million bales in 1995/96.
* Tea production forecast to rise to 790 million kg in 1996/97 from 762.4 million in 1995/96.
* Coffee output in 1996/97 expected to be 220,000 tonnes compared with 223,000 in the previous year.
* Rubber output in 1996/97 forecast at 542,000 tonnes against 507,000 tonnes in the same period in 1995/96.
* Fertilisers output in 1996/97 expected to be 11.7 million tonnes against 11.3 million in 1995/96.
